tonight.headline: 40.8–0, and Panda Attack banked 22.5 on their own bench.
body: Josh Allen's 40.8 is still the only score in this matchup and it is the second-best quarterback week of the slate. Panda Attack's one Thursday player was Dalton Kincaid, who scored 22.5 — from slot 20. They left it on the bench and it does not count. That is a 22.5-point gift and it is the entire reason a 59% win probability is not higher.
Nothing you do in the next eleven hours changes that lead. What you can change is the tight end seat behind it: Baltimore kick at 11:00 your time and Mark Andrews is a free agent until then.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Panda Attack start Dak Prescott, George Pickens and Javonte Williams in the Dallas–Washington 20:25 window and Chase Brown plus Saquon Barkley at 17:00. That is 70-odd projected points from five starters in two games. If Dallas and Philadelphia both run away with theirs, they clear 125 without needing anything strange.

case.label: Why you are still favoured
case.body: You have 40.8 banked against their zero and a Monday-night tight end they cannot cover. Their only remaining leverage is volume on Sunday afternoon; yours is a lead plus an extra game.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Achane at San Francisco is the swing. Miami are 13.5-point underdogs, which caps his carries even as full PPR pays him for the catches a blowout produces. If he lands under ten, the 59% is optimistic.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Baltimore kick 11:00 Mexico City · free agent, no priority spent
doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mark Andrews
doFirst.subtitle: Third run carrying this card. The one thing it hinged on resolved in its favour overnight: Zay Flowers is officially out.

case.label: The condition that resolved
case.body: This card was published twice with an explicit hold clause: if Zay Flowers appeared ACTIVE on Sunday's list, it became a hold. BaltimoreRavens.com ruled him out yesterday — hamstring, carried from the opener where he put up 150 yards and a touchdown. The clause did not trip. The card is live.

case.label: The player you are getting
case.body: Andrews tied Flowers for the team-high six targets in Week 1 even with Flowers healthy, and caught four for 49. Sports Illustrated's read with Flowers out: that number rises and he becomes Lamar Jackson's go-to, a must-start. New Orleans allowed Sam LaPorta five catches on eight targets in Week 1, so the draw is right too.

case.label: The drop, on the record
case.body: Pitts is 93.3% rostered and dropping anyone above half needs a stated disagreement with the market. Here it is. Atlanta named Cooper Rush the starter again yesterday with Michael Penix Jr. ruled out for a second week — NFL.com and AtlantaFalcons.com both. Pitts is a tight end catching passes from a third-string quarterback, and Chem's flex is RB/WR only, so he cannot reach your lineup in any week this season no matter what he does.

case.label: What this does not change
case.body: Isaiah Likely keeps the tight end slot. He is TE5, went 8-for-8 with two touchdowns in Week 1, and plays Monday night. Andrews replaces Pitts as the second tight end, not Likely as the first. Chem gives a second tight end no lineup path, so this is an upgrade of a dead seat, not a new one.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Baltimore redistribute outward rather than inward — the Ravens' own site says Rashod Bateman moves into the top receiver spot with Flowers out, and if Bateman clears seven targets while Andrews stays at four or five, the target vacuum went to the perimeter and this card was the wrong read of the same injury.

doFirst.title: Kyle Monangai for Jaylen Warren at RB2 — still unarmed, third run running
doFirst.subtitle: Kept on the board because the snap count that created it is real. Not fired, because the touches that decide it point the other way.

case.label: The number that made this card
case.body: DraftSharks on Week 1: Rico Dowdle took a 58% snap share, ran 20 routes and played nine third-down snaps. Warren played 17 early-down snaps and two on third down. On snaps alone Warren is the second back in Pittsburgh and this brief graded him on carries for two runs without saying so.

case.label: The column that keeps it unarmed
case.body: Touches went the other way. Warren had 15 to Dowdle's 10, six targets to Dowdle's two, and both short-yardage carries. In full PPR five catches is five points before a yard is gained. Sports Illustrated have Warren RB24 and Dowdle RB27 on a near-even split, and FantasyPros make Warren an RB2 this week against what they call New England's permissive run defence.

case.label: Why not just swap anyway
case.body: Monangai projects 9.9 to Warren's 11.4. STRATEGY calls a move that lowers projected points a hard floor that needs a role reason, and Monangai does not have one this week — D'Andre Swift is active and Chicago's backs split the work in a 59-point game.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Dowdle out-touches Warren at New England today. That is the second consecutive week of the snap share and the touch share disagreeing, it fires Warren's own clause, and the RB2 seat opens on Tuesday rather than staying closed.

whatWentWrong.title: Your bench tight end is behind a third-string quarterback, and Atlanta confirmed it again yesterday
whatWentWrong.lead: Michael Penix Jr. was ruled out for a second straight week and Cooper Rush was named the starter. Pitts projects 10.4 anyway.

case.label: What was confirmed
case.body: NFL.com and AtlantaFalcons.com both carried it yesterday: Rush starts against Carolina, Penix out again. This is the second week running that Atlanta's projection for Pitts has been computed as though a starting quarterback were throwing to him.

case.label: Why it matters more than the number
case.body: This is the exact failure the runbook was built around — a tight end projected 9.8 and scored 0.0 behind Atlanta's third-stringer while a startable alternative sat on the bench. The projection has not learned. The brief has.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: It is the drop half of the Andrews card above. Nothing else — Pitts cannot enter your flex, so he was never going to play for you regardless of who throws.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Atlanta elevate Penix on Sunday morning and Pitts clears five targets, which would say the Rush discount is being over-applied and that a 93% rostered tight end was dropped on a two-week sample.

whatWentWrong.title: The Steelers snap counts say Dowdle leads that backfield, and your RB2 is the other guy
whatWentWrong.lead: 58% to 35.9% on snaps, 20 routes to Warren's handful. Warren still out-touched him 15 to 10 and out-targeted him 6 to 2.

case.label: Both things are true
case.body: DraftSharks have Dowdle at a 58% snap share with nine third-down snaps against Warren's two. Yet Warren took both short-yardage carries, caught five of six, and finished as the better fantasy back. Mike Tomlin's staff have said both will play and both matter.

case.label: Why this is a warning and not an action
case.body: A back who loses the goal line and passing downs is uniquely bad in full PPR. Warren has lost neither yet — he has lost the snap count. Those are different problems and only one of them is fatal.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: It keeps the Monangai card on the board unarmed rather than deleting it, and it sets today's game as the tiebreak.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Dowdle taking the short-yardage work or the target edge today. Either one turns a snap-share complaint into a role loss and the RB2 seat opens Tuesday.

worthALook.name: Rashod Bateman
worthALook.lead: Moved off Do-not-chase. The Ravens' own website now says he takes the top receiver spot with Flowers out, and that contradicts the number this brief has been killing him with.

case.label: What changed overnight
case.body: BaltimoreRavens.com, ruling Flowers out: 'Rashod Bateman will move into the top receiver spot,' with Wester, Walker, Moore and Sarratt absorbing the rest. That is the team saying it, not an aggregator inferring it.

case.label: The number that still argues against
case.body: In Week 1 with Flowers healthy Bateman ran a 4.2% target share. This brief published that as the case-killer two runs ago and it was the right number then. It is a statement about a role he no longer has.

case.label: Which side I take
case.body: The team's. A 4.2% share measured behind a healthy Flowers tells you nothing about the share behind an absent one, and +5.36 ownership in a single day says the wider market read the same announcement. But I am not spending a roster spot on it, because the Andrews card is the same bet with a better price and an actual seat.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Bateman under five targets today. That says Baltimore funnelled the vacated work to Andrews inside rather than outside, which confirms the Andrews card and closes this row for good. Seven or more and he is a free claim on Tuesday — Chem priority resets weekly, so it costs nothing lasting.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: Still the largest receiver ownership anomaly on this board and still a free agent. Today decides whether he is also the answer to your Brian Thomas problem.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on the Chem wire, at 76.7% rostered nationally and free here. STRATEGY section 4 ranks widely-rostered-elsewhere-and-free-here as the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league.

case.label: The health question, answered
case.body: NBC Sports: the thumb is cleared and he was removed from Jacksonville's injury report entirely. He plays at Denver today.

case.label: Why not now
case.body: There is no seat. The tight end seat is spoken for by the Andrews card and every other bench spot holds someone with an intact thesis. Adding a fifth receiver to a roster that starts three is the churn STRATEGY section 3 exists to prevent.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Meyers out-targets Brian Thomas Jr. at Denver today while Thomas is shadowed by Surtain, the swap is Meyers for Thomas on Tuesday — Thomas's own thesis is the one that broke, so no third player is involved. If Thomas wins the day, this row closes.

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: On waivers until Wednesday, which is after his game. Whatever the sleeper note was about, it is spent before you could ever act on it.

case.label: The timing problem
case.body: He clears 07:00Z on 23 September. Buffalo already played Thursday. Anything a Week 2 note promised has happened, and the claim would buy you a Week 3 asset priced on Week 2 hype.

case.label: Why the row stays
case.body: Chem priority resets weekly, so a Wednesday claim costs nothing lasting. The question is only whether he is worth a roster spot by then, and that is a question Week 2 answers rather than asks.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Six or more targets in the Detroit game makes him a free claim on Wednesday. Under six and the note was about game script, not role, and this row closes.

doNotChase.name: Jordan Addison
doNotChase.lead: A 171.4 season projection and free here, and the reason is sitting in the Minnesota quarterback room.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Sports Illustrated's Wentz-start rankings put Addison at WR60 and say plainly that Wentz is unlikely to support two viable receivers. Jefferson is described as the only player you can start on Minnesota.

case.label: Why the anomaly is not a discovery
case.body: Recorded so a future run does not rediscover it. He was dropped inside this league on 16 September by JuiceJam, which is why he is free — not because the market blundered.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wentz clearing 250 passing yards with Addison above a 20% target share, or Kyler Murray clearing concussion protocol for Week 3. Either reopens him, cheaply, since priority resets.

doNotChase.name: Rachaad White
doNotChase.lead: Top why=OWNED back on this wire at 66.0%, and a committee body underneath it.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 27 offensive snaps in his Commanders debut against Jacory Croskey-Merritt's 33. He is the second back in a committee that has not settled, on a team whose receiver is the reason you care about Washington at all.

case.label: Where he actually matters to you
case.body: He is Team 13's second starting running back in your other league, which is what makes the Lamar trade there work. His value to AVIATO is as a fact about someone else's roster.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Croskey-Merritt missing a game, or White clearing five targets in a week. Either turns a committee body into a role.

doNotChase.name: Xavier Worthy
doNotChase.lead: 74.2% rostered nationally and free here, and the reason is how Kansas City are throwing rather than who is catching.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Three catches on six targets in Week 1 with 76.9% of his snaps out wide, graded a WR4 because Mahomes averaged 1.1 air yards per attempt. A deep receiver on a checkdown offence is a projection, not a role.

case.label: The branch that is closed
case.body: The upside case was Rashee Rice missing time. Rice is off Kansas City's injury report and starts tonight against Indianapolis, so that branch is shut.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Kansas City's air-yards profile normalising across two weeks. Tonight's game against a Colts defence that ran 46.9% man in Week 1 is the first real test of it.

case.label: What would change it

cannotSee.label: This run fired at the wrong hour and the roster is unlocked, not locked
cannotSee.body: The schedule describes a 16:00 Mexico City refresh with most players locked. It actually fired at 23:50 Saturday. Every recommendation here was written for a pre-slate roster, because that is what the data shows: one game played, thirteen to come.

cannotSee.label: Positional defence ranks barely exist two games in
cannotSee.body: The runbook grades from an opponent's season rank in points allowed to a position. After one week that rank is one game. Every grade here rests on reporting — a shadow assignment, a spread, a pass-rush number — and says so in its evidence line. Six rows are dashed because even that was not available.

cannotSee.label: Whether Rashod Bateman or Mark Andrews absorbs the Flowers targets
cannotSee.body: They are the same bet read in opposite directions and I have taken the inside one. The Ravens' statement supports Bateman; Week 1's six targets and the LaPorta comparison support Andrews. Today settles it and one of the two rows in this brief is wrong.

cannotSee.label: Miami's starting quarterback, for a second run
cannotSee.body: I could not retrieve a Week 2 confirmation. NFL.com has Quinn Ewers taking over the starting role for 2026; a Yahoo column has him opening 2026 as the backup. Achane is a running back so the grade does not turn on it, but his receiving volume does, and I am not going to guess.

cannotSee.label: Season projections are still frozen
cannotSee.body: seasonProj returned the same figures as the 17 September snapshot. The trade search that found nothing is priced on a field that may be a preseason artifact. The conclusion happens to be robust — zero pairs, not marginal ones — but the arithmetic underneath it is not proven live.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending waiver claims are invisible
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own. Mark Andrews is a free agent this morning, which means anyone can take him before 11:00 without warning, and you would see it only after the fact.

cannotSee.label: One of your starters plays Monday and one has already played
cannotSee.body: Josh Allen is banked at 40.8 and Isaiah Likely does not kick off until Monday 18:15. Your matchup will look decided on Sunday night and will not be.

cannotSee.label: The Chem trade section is empty and that is a finding
cannotSee.body: It is not an omission. Every one-for-one pair across all nine opposing rosters was scored on both sides' optimal lineups this morning and none gained for both teams. The section is empty because the market is, not because nobody looked.
